item.title: The Plastic Country
item.description:
Wed 9 Sep, 6:00 PM · Brunswick Picture House, Brunswick Heads NSW · GENERAL — Free screening but registration mandatory
Join us for a special screening of The Plastic Country , a powerful new Australian documentary that uncovers the true scale of our nation’s plastic crisis and its impacts on our environment, wildlife, and human health. A panel with the filmmaker, some local ocean advocates and community changemakers will follow the screening. Following filmmaker and ocean advocate Kal Glanznig, The Plastic Country takes audiences on a remarkable journey across Australia, from the remote shores of East Arnhem Land to bustling urban waterways and the halls of Parliament House. Along the way, Kal meets scientists, Traditional Owners, wildlife carers, campaigners and industry leaders who reveal how deeply plastic pollution has infiltrated our ecosystems and increasingly, our own bodies. Filmed over two years and featuring music from acclaimed First Nations band King Stingray, the documentary blends breathtaking Australian landscapes with personal storytelling and investigative journalism to explore one of the most pressing environmental and public health challenges of our time. Australia is one of the highest producers of plastic waste per person in the world, with Australians using around three times the global average amount of plastic. The Plastic Country shines a light on the consequences of this dependence while highlighting practical solutions that are already helping reduce plastic pollution and create a more sustainable future. More than a documentary, The Plastic Country is a call to action. It aims to shift the conversation around plastic pollution from a distant environmental concern to an urgent human health and policy issue, encouraging stronger action to reduce plastic production, support reusable alternatives, and prevent waste at its source. Whether you’re passionate about protecting our oceans, concerned about human health, or interested in creating positive change in your community, this screening offers an inspiring and eye-opening opportunity to learn, reflect and take action. Come along, be informed, and discover how together we can help turn the tide on plastic pollution.

item.title: Michael Hing: How Are We Supposed To Live Like This?
item.description:
Fri 11 Sep, 7:00 AM · Brunswick Picture House, Brunswick Heads NSW · GENERAL — $38 (inclusive of booking fee)
Life is increasingly insane. Nothing makes sense. Everything is chaos, and we’re all just expected to keep on going? The planet is on fire, money is imaginary, we are ruled over by a moronic class of preening narcissists, but every day you’re just meant to go to work and come home and pretend you don’t notice that we’re being gouged at every corner and there are fewer and fewer Arnott’s shapes in every packet. Unrelated to all this, Michael Hing is developing a brand new hour of comedy.

item.description:
Sun 13 Sep, 4:00 PM · Hotel Brunswick · See link
SUB-TRIBE LIVE AT HOTEL BRUNSWICK SUNDAY 13 SEPTEMBER | FROM 4PM | FREE EVENT From the roots of Aotearoa (New Zealand) comes SUB-TRIBE — a 7-piece dub-fusion powerhouse delivering heavy bass, glitchy beats and soaring harmonies. Blending blues-soaked dub, chunky skank reggae, jazz-hop and ragga dancehall, SUB-TRIBE take audiences on a genre-hopping journey that keeps dancefloors moving and heads nodding. Known for their high-energy live shows and feel-good vibes, SUB-TRIBE have carved out a sound often described as “Unprecedented Dub-Fusion.” Since forming in 2017 and touring alongside Salmonella Dub, the band has built a strong reputation across Australia and New Zealand, appearing at major festivals including WOMADelaide, Good Love Festival, Kuranda Roots and Island Vibes. With releases spanning deep, rolling dub, soulful lovers rock and bass-driven dancefloor anthems, SUB-TRIBE bring a live show that’s equal parts groove, grit and celebration. w/ support | Free Entry Come skank, sway and get deep in the low end.

item.title: Colours of Time
item.description:
Sun 20 Sep · Star Court Theatre · $18/$15
Brought together by the unexpected inheritance of an abandoned house in rural Normandy, four cousins discover they share a mysterious family history. In 1895, their ancestor Adèle, then aged 21, leaves her hometown to search for her mother in Paris. She discovers a city on the cusp of modernity, bustling with new-found avant-garde creativity, with the rise of photography and the birth of Impressionist painting. As her descendants retrace her steps, they unravel Adèle’s surprising past. The two timelines of 1895 and 2024 intertwine and collide, confronting the cousins’ contemporary attitudes with life in late 19th century Paris, leaving everyone’s future forever changed.

item.title: Ben Whiting
item.description:
Thu 17 Sep, 6:00 PM · Hotel Brunswick · See link
BEN WHITING | Hotel Brunswick | Thursday 17 September 6pm An alluring voice with rock beneath the surface Ben Whiting is a seasoned singer-songwriter whose sound blends sun-soaked reggae grooves, classic rock grit and thoughtful folk songwriting. Raised on a steady diet of The Police and Bob Marley, and shaped by years of jamming, touring and festival stages, Whiting delivers music that feels both familiar and entirely his own. With a “virtually flawless” voice (Faster Louder) at the centre, his live shows move effortlessly between laid-back rhythms, soaring melodies and dynamic rock moments. Having previously played major festivals including Splendour In The Grass and shared stages with artists like Katy Perry, Grinspoon and The Angels, Whiting brings a confident, polished performance that suits both relaxed afternoon sessions and attentive listeners alike. Expect warm grooves, rich vocals and songs that stay with you. Live at Hotel Brunswick 📅 Thursday 17 September 🕑 6:00pm | Free Gig
